items.title: Two different ballgames sharing one game_pk — and one line
items.tagline: Not a bad price: a bad LINE. The consensus total is a median across books, so pooling two games under one game_pk moved the number a pick is made and graded at to one neither market posted. A pick was served UNDER 12.5 on a game whose market ran 8.5-9.5.
items.latest: 2026-08-01: found by accident, two weeks late, while investigating the stale-quote defect. 580 (game_pk, snapshot) cells since 2026-07-18 carried two different odds_event_ids on one game_pk, across FOUR games (823518, 824412, 824489, 824732) — plus a fifth, 823357 (2026-07-10), whose two events never share a snapshot and so contributed zero cells and would have been missed by any cell-based count. MECHANISM, evidenced, two compounding causes: all four are game 2 of a SPLIT DOUBLEHEADER whose game 1 was the makeup of a game rained out the day before. MLB's schedule endpoint lists a postponed game on BOTH dates — its original date at its original first pitch, and the makeup date at the new one — and collect_forward_odds._schedule_window deduped by game_pk FIRST-WINS while iterating dates ascending, so the STALE listing won and the makeup game entered the matcher ~18h from where it actually was. odds/backfill.make_matcher then had nothing near the orphaned makeup event except its doubleheader partner and accepted it, because its tolerance was SIX HOURS and the matcher was many-to-one: nothing forbade two events claiming one game_pk. Every foreign event sat 5h29m-5h59m out — the 31-minute band immediately under the old 6h tolerance. 823357 is a second variant: a suspended game resumed the next day, for which the Odds API opened a second event. Same family as the 2021-2023 GAME_PK_CONTAMINATION_AUDIT, whose 2026-07-28 addendum adopted a 3h rule for the other three stores; this store was not in that pass. BLAST RADIUS, exact: recomputing all five walls per game merged vs single-event reproduced fact_serve.parquet EXACTLY on all 19 rows, so the merge is the whole cause. 14 (game x wall x market) consensus cells moved — worst 824489 T-3h totals 12.5 vs a true 9.0 (+3.5), 824412 T-1h run line +5.5 vs +1.5, and five run-line cells that SIGN-FLIPPED favourite and underdog. 823518's two games happened to sit on the same number so nothing moved there, which is exactly why this needed a rail and not an eyeball. Served: 19 fact_serve rows (1.27%), 9 of 24 graded/ledger rows, 27 of 36 farm rows, 12 of 16 analyst-v2 rows. ACTUAL BETS: exactly ONE served PICK sits on a corrupted line — 824732 T-12h OVER 9.0, 4 stars, graded LOSS — and 9.0 was a number real books posted on that game (the true consensus was 8.75, a between-books median), so NO bet was graded against a line no book posted. Under the fix that row becomes unpriceable (no book at 8.75) and would never have been a bet at all. THE NEAR MISS, stated plainly: 824489 T-3h was pick_side=under, pick_line=12.5, take=true, tier=Strong, +140, graded result=WIN at graded_line=12.5, on a game whose own market ran 8.5-9.5 at 23 books all day — the 12.5 came from the other game's books, which were by then quoting it IN PLAY. It reached the payload as PASS only because an unrelated evidence gate (junk_cell) demoted it. Nothing in the pipeline knew the line was fictional. Nothing was repaired: write-once is absolute, every affected board row is already locked, and no row was re-priced, re-lined or re-graded.
items.detail: THE RULE, added as CLAUSE 0 of the price-validity rule in v4/assemble/price_validity.py and therefore stated once: every quote used for a game — to build its consensus LINE and to price it — must come from ONE odds event, i.e. one actual ballgame. This clause is logically PRIOR to the other three, which all reason about 'the pick's own line'; there is no such thing until the game has exactly one market. RESOLUTION, not merging: one event -> that one; more than one with exactly one inside 180 minutes of scheduled first pitch -> that one; anything else (zero candidates, two or more, or no first pitch to judge by) -> MERGED_MARKET, which is UNPRICEABLE and also UNLINEABLE — the consensus comes back None, not a best effort, so rolling_engine writes market_line=pick_line=None and ev_gate returns take=false / PASS / no_price. A merged market therefore cannot become a bet by construction rather than by anyone remembering to check. A LONE event is never drift-checked: game_label.first_pitch_utc is itself never updated on reschedule (upsert_label's ON CONFLICT does not touch date or first_pitch_utc), and voiding a game's only market because our own schedule row aged would invent a defect that is not in the odds. THE WINDOW IS NOT THE LOAD-BEARING PART, and the measurement says so honestly: over 407 (game, event) pairs since 2026-07-01, 94.1% sit within 30 minutes of first pitch (p50 1.0 min, p90 5.0 min), but the separation is NOT clean — four legitimate single-event games sit 222-299 minutes out, the worst outliers sit weeks out on stale game_label rows, and 824412's foreign event sits at 179 minutes, INSIDE the window. No threshold cleanly partitions own-event from foreign-event, and any nearest-wins rule would still get 824412 wrong. So the window is a CANDIDATE FILTER and uniqueness is the rule: the window must leave exactly one survivor or the row is refused. On the real store this resolves 823518, 824489 and 824732 to their correct event at every wall (824489 T-3h totals 12.5 -> 9.0, run line stops sign-flipping) and REFUSES 824412 outright — the honest answer, because its own first_pitch_utc is stale (20:10Z against a real 23:10Z) and all three of its events sit within 3h of the only anchor available. All four doubleheader partners (824414, 824490, 823519, 824735) price separately and correctly off their own events. FIXED AT SOURCE so the store stops acquiring the condition: odds/backfill MATCH_TOL 6h -> 3h plus _resolve_event_claims, which enforces ONE EVENT PER GAME across a whole payload — when N events claim one game_pk the nearest keeps it and the rest are stored with game_pk=NULL (which the schema already documents as 'unmatched to MLB schedule') rather than merged; and collect_forward_odds._schedule_window now takes the LAST listing rather than the first and drops Postponed games from the candidate set. THE PRICE-CONVENTION MARKER DELIBERATELY DOES NOT MOVE: clause 0 never chooses a different price, it either admits the row (price bit-identical to v3) or voids it, so bumping to v4 would push every currently-served v3 row into the rail's older-convention arm and demote live picks with nothing wrong with them — restating the product to record a distinction that does not exist. Coherence is stamped per row instead (odds_market_coherent, odds_event_id_resolved, odds_n_events, odds_unpriceable_reason). THE RAIL, because this slipped in on 2026-07-18 and was found on 2026-08-01 by accident: price_validity.merged_market_scan fails loudly when a game's quotes span more than one market, naming each event, its commence, its row count and its drift. daily_cycle.market_coherence_rail runs it on the board's own games EVERY intraday cycle and publishes under daily_cycle_report.json -> market_coherence whether or not it fires, so its silence is evidence that it ran; unified_model._selftest check 11b runs it against the real store with a NEGATIVE CONTROL proving the scanner still detects the known-merged games. A RESOLVABLE merge still fails the rail — 'the fix would price it right' is not a reason for the store to contain it. The scan reads MIN(commence_time), not MAX: books restate commence forward once a game is in play, and on 824412 a MAX would name the foreign event as the true one. Selftests: odds_features fixture 9 covers both required shapes end to end against an odds_snapshots-shaped store — two event ids on one game_pk (priced off the game's own event when the anchor discriminates, REFUSED outright when it cannot) and a genuine doubleheader (both games priced, separately, on different lines) — plus a negative control and a lone-event-with-stale-anchor case; backfill.py --selftest covers the collector invariant. DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED and named rather than fixed quietly: champion_v2.latest_per_side_price (read-only by standing rule; the champion had NO_VIEW on all five games) and pregame_line.current_pregame_market (display-side).
items.result: Live. Merged markets are unpriceable AND unlineable; the collector can no longer create the condition; a rail runs every intraday cycle and in the serving selftest. unified_model 781 pass / 0 fail (was 756 / 0; +25 new checks). Served games[].pick and record.headline_champion_v2 are byte-identical on rebuild, proven by checksum. Five pre-fix games are disclosed and untouched; one of them (824412) is now honestly unpriceable rather than wrong.

items.title: A price from a book that had already left the market
items.tagline: The third and last defect in the pricing family: the number was at our line, in our market, and quoted by a book that had stopped posting two hours earlier. One rule now covers all three.
items.latest: 2026-08-01: found on game 823594 (MIA @ NYM). The T-24h row was priced UNDER 9.0 at -107 from lowvig — whose last quote for that game was 18:26Z, one hour and forty-four minutes before the T-24h wall. In the snapshot at the wall lowvig was not in the market at all and the best real UNDER 9.0 was -110. The price builder collapses every snapshot up to the wall to each book's last quote, which is right for market-structure features and wrong for an executable price: it resurrects departed books and lets them win the best-price contest. BLAST RADIUS, measured before the fix: 2.21% of at-line price cells (77 of 3,492 game x wall x side over July) were won by a book that had left, faking a payout +2.38% richer on average and +48.6% at worst. On rows we actually served: 3 of 110 priced rows on today's board and 5 of 889 in the write-once served-day store, none of them bets; across all graded history 14 rows and FOUR actual bets (2026-07-19 823521 OVER 7.5 at +100 against a live -105; 2026-07-21 824085 OVER 9.5 at +100 against -110; 2026-07-25 823679 OVER 10.5 at -102 against -104; 2026-07-25 823027 OVER 8.5 at +100 with no live quote at our line at all, which under the fix makes it unpriceable and therefore never a bet). All four lost. Nothing was repaired: write-once is absolute and every one of them keeps the price it was served at.
items.detail: THE RULE, now stated once and enforced in one place (v4/assemble/price_validity.py): a served price must be simultaneously AT THE PICK'S OWN LINE, from the FULL-GAME market, and LIVE AT THE DECISION WALL — present in the latest snapshot at or before the wall, from a book actually posting then. The three defects in this family each broke exactly one clause: the price came from a book on a different number (fixed 07-31), the line was read from the in-play remaining-runs market (fixed 07-30), and now the price was a stale quote from a departed book. THE TOLERANCE WAS MEASURED, NOT PICKED: across 22,562 (game x wall x book) cells in July, 96.6% of books are present in the reference snapshot itself and NOTHING sits between 0 and 5 minutes of staleness — the collector polls every book on a 10-minute cadence, so a book has either just quoted or missed a whole cycle. And a book that missed a cycle is usually gone: 'never quotes again before first pitch' runs 78-92% at 5-15 minutes and 81-86% past two hours, against 1.6% for books in the reference snapshot; even the returners bring the identical line and price only 0-53% of the time against 88.7%. The tolerance is therefore 2 minutes, an epsilon for duplicate snapshot ids rather than a grace period, and it admits exactly the same set as zero on the measurement. NO FALLBACK: when no live book is on the pick's line the row is unpriceable and ev_gate refuses to make it a bet, identical to the handling of 'no book at the line at all'. The consensus LINE is still computed over every book, so freshness can never move the number a pick is graded at. Book-level freshness does not replace the snapshot-level odds_snapshot_age_min / odds_stale signals, which stay as published disclosures; the 88 of 1,500 rows (5.9%) sitting on a reference snapshot hours older than their wall are a separate, larger question and are named as such rather than folded in quietly. The rail now reports the CAUSE — wrong line, wrong market, or stale quote, with the book and the age — so the next instance of this family diagnoses itself instead of arriving as a mystery.
items.result: Live. Prices are convention-marked best_at_pick_line_live_v3; rows built under the older marker are demoted if still pregame and disclosed if frozen, never re-priced. Served picks and the published champion record are byte-identical, proven by checksum.

items.title: Every analyst files on every game, at every wall — the evidence floor is retired
items.tagline: A missing lever now takes its neutral value and contributes exactly nothing, instead of silencing the analyst. Four reads on every game on the board; the honesty moved from the empty chair onto the read itself.
items.latest: 2026-08-01: Leon, on seeing 'no plate assignment yet' on the board — 'ALL models need to run!!'. He is right: a desk with empty chairs is not a desk. The old design refused to file when an analyst's inputs were thin (an evidence floor of 50% of the wall model's |beta| mass over at least two levers) and served the seat empty with a stated reason. That is now replaced by GRACEFUL DEGRADATION, and the honest part is that nothing is invented. In an additive model a missing lever has a well-defined neutral value: engines.neutral_mask zeroes its standardised value (the train median standardises to exactly 0) and engines.absent_center_correction adds back its share of the contemporaneous centre, so its contribution to the DEVIATION the analyst actually bets is exactly 0.00 runs — not approximately nothing. That second half matters and was a real bug: without it a missing umpire pushed ATLAS toward the side opposite the average umpire, a contribution made by information it did not have. Measured consequence: a FULLY-INFORMED read is bit-for-bit what the engine produced before any of this existed (45 of 45 complete reads on a settled slate reprice identically, and it is a selftest); only reads with genuinely missing levers move. WHAT SURVIVES IS ALL OF THE HONESTY: every read publishes information_completeness, completeness_tier, levers_neutral_filled and a plain completeness_note; a neutral-filled lever still cannot be cited (citable_drivers unchanged) and now cannot be DESCRIBED either — the take library gained a per-LEVER gate beside its information-class gate, so ATLAS may not say 'park, altitude, roof' on a read whose park row never landed; and conviction is reduced by the information rather than only the point estimate, through confidence_scale = sqrt(completeness), which is exactly 1 at full information. MEASURED ON THE 2026-08-01 SLATE: 236 of 236 (analyst x wall) seats file a side, against 3 the retired floor would have silenced; mean completeness by wall VEGA 100/100/100/100/100%, SCOUT 100/100/100/100/100%, NOVA 100/100/100/93/93%, ATLAS 70/77/78/85/85% — the umpire arriving late is the whole of ATLAS's shape, and it is now visible on the read instead of deleting it. The board went from 16 of 17 games fully read to 20 of 20.
items.detail: Files: v4/models/analyst_v2/availability.py (the floor becomes a measurement), v4/models/analyst_v2/engines.py (neutral_mask, zmatrix(mask), rolling_center_components, absent_center_correction, confidence_scale, the stated tie-break), v4/serve/analyst_v2_walls.py and v4/serve/analyst_v2_stream.py (both boards), v4/serve/analyst_takes.py (the lever gate + a degraded voice per analyst + SCOUT's missing 'no starters named' line), v4/serve/analyst_desk.py (the completeness on the seat). WRITE-ONCE IS UNCHANGED AND ABSOLUTE for a read: a written read is frozen for ever. A STATED REFUSAL is not an opinion and was never graded, so a seat the retired floor left empty may be filled by the analyst's real read exactly once, one-way, and only on dates from 2026-08-01. The 126 seats the floor left empty in July stay empty on purpose — the per-wall record published over those dates was computed on that population, and filling them would move a published number. That is a selftested constant.
items.result: 236/236 seats file a side on the live slate; 0 analyst abstentions at any wall from T-24h on. record.analysts and the per-wall records are byte-unchanged; games[].pick and record.headline_champion_v2 are byte-unchanged. NO PERFORMANCE CLAIM: the standing hygiene rule applies in full — this is a coverage and honesty change, not evidence of edge.

items.title: The desk makes a call on every game — and a call is never a bet
items.tagline: AVOID showed on 13 of 17 games because AVOID means 'no bet cleared the price gate'. The desk had a view on all of them. The two are now separate products: a directional call on every game, and a bet that stays exactly as strict.
items.latest: 2026-08-01: the product was conflating two questions. WHAT DOES THE DESK THINK is a directional view that exists on every game; WHETHER WE ARE BETTING IT is the price gate, and after the pricing fix very few games clear it. Silence on 13 of 17 cards was the result. They are now separate axes on the same card. THE CALL: games[].diamondedge.desk_call — a side, a conviction (STRONG/CLEAR/SLIGHT), the desk's own probability and a one-line argument, on every game. It is the equal-weight mean of the four analysts' own p_over, which is not a shortcut but the measured house position: desk_fit fitted four weights on 311 graded games and its walk-forward REFUSED them (dLL -0.00026, 95% CI [-0.00145, +0.00084]), so equal_weight_fallback is what the desk is entitled to use. Each analyst's p_over already carries its own information completeness after the same day's graceful-degradation work, so a thin desk produces a visibly less convinced call with no extra machinery. The vote is reported beside the probability and is NOT decisive; when a loud minority carries the call the row says the head-count went the other way. THE BET: games[].diamondedge.action is untouched — PLAY / LEAN / AVOID, with AVOID still meaning, and only ever meaning, that no bet was served. The +EV gate does not move by one basis point. On the 2026-08-01 board: 15 CALL_NO_BET, 3 CALL_AND_LEAN, 2 CALL_AND_PLAY — 20 of 20 games with a decisive call, where 15 of 20 used to be a silent AVOID.
items.detail: New module v4/serve/desk_call.py with its own three stores (desk_call_board.json write-once per (date, game, wall), desk_call_graded.jsonl append-only, desk_call_record.json). A CALL IS NEVER A BET BY CONSTRUCTION: enforce_never_a_bet() is the only row constructor and hard-stamps is_bet/staked/playable/take/is_pick false and stake_units/suggested_units/stars/ev/score/pick_side null; _assert_never_a_bet() re-checks on every write AND every read AND at the serving boundary AND on the history projection; _assert_own_store() refuses every served board and product ledger BY NAME. The graded product remains games[].pick and only games[].pick — the call ledger carries no units and no ROI, because a call has no price. Published at record.desk_calls and documented at analyst_desk_spec.call_vocabulary; wired into daily_cycle at step 3g5 (freeze every serve, grade + record overnight), WARN-never-block.
items.result: 20/20 games carry a desk call; the bet axis is unchanged (15 AVOID / 3 LEAN / 2 PLAY). games[].pick byte-identical on the live board and record.overall / record.overall_playable / record.headline_champion_v2 byte-identical everywhere. The call ledger starts 2026-08-01 and, per the standing hygiene rule, will take months to say anything — and a call rate above 50% is explicitly NOT an argument for loosening the gate.

items.title: The pattern engine stops describing four analysts that no longer exist
items.tagline: record.patterns was the last surface still deriving the desk's four sides from the pre-re-architecture ledgers. It now reads the v2 stream, on 331 games — and the answer is a null, with the two rows that look striking failing correction exactly as designed.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: repointed, the same repointing record.consensus_history got earlier today, one module over. v4/serve/consensus_patterns.py was still assembling its four sides from the champion ledger, the model grid, the simulator stream, the fundamentals stream and the walk-forward reconstruction in v4/models/analyst_desk/history.parquet — five stores that all describe the analysts dismantled on 2026-07-31. It now reads the v2 stream and nothing else: sides through the published chief contract analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date(), results off the append-only v2 graded ledger's own stored final. A selftest proves every side in the table is byte-identical to what reads_for_date() serves the chief, and a structural check asserts no module-level path resolves to a legacy store any more. THE TABLE, on 331 reconstructed games (2026-07-01 → 07-30): all four agree 22-38-5, 36.7% (95% CI 24.6-50.1%, n=60 decided, p=0.052); a 3-1 majority 72-74-0, 49.3% (41.0-57.7%, n=146, p=0.93); a 2-2 split 46-72-2, 39.0% (30.1-48.4%, n=118, p=0.021). The live era is a separate block at 1 game and the two are never summed. THE HEADLINE IS A NULL: across the 41 rows the table renders, ZERO survive Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.10. Four rows clear 50% on their own uncorrected interval — the strongest is a 2-2 split with ATLAS+NOVA on the over at 24.0% on n=25, raw p=0.0146 against the 0.00244 it had to beat — which is what testing 41 overlapping buckets at 95% produces by chance, and is exactly why the correction is there. `highlights` is [] and the surface leads with the null, not an empty state.
items.detail: READ THE DISTRIBUTION SHIFT CORRECTLY: IT IS NOT A RESULT. Every cell in this table looks nothing like its predecessor, because the re-architecture decorrelated the four on purpose. Measured on the new corpus, pairwise side agreement is 0.512-0.572 (it was 0.84-0.89), and all sixteen configurations now occur where most previously never did. A differently populated bucket is not a better or worse one. The corpus also shrank from thousands of reconstructed games to 332, because it restarts at 2026-07-01 — the day after the training fence — and a selftest now asserts that not one frame sits on or before 2026-06-30, since a pattern measured on the data these models were fitted on would be a fabrication rather than a weak result. THE ANTI-CHERRY-PICKING DISCIPLINE WAS REBUILT INTO THE NEW SOURCE, NOT RE-DERIVED: one Benjamini-Hochberg pass across the entire rendered family and never per bucket; only survivors may be presented, ordered by evidence and never by effect size; every rendered sentence carries its exact interval inside it; cells under the minimum n are ineligible; and the two eras are computed, labelled and rendered apart. Both counter-fixtures still hold: a purely random 1,200-game desk whose most deviant cell sits 11.8 points off 50% emits ZERO findings, and a planted 62% effect on n=800 still opens the gate and is emitted with its interval in the sentence — so the gate is a filter, not a blanket veto. One thing was tightened rather than preserved: the null headline used to assert that every interval includes 50%, which was true of the old corpus and is not true of this one, and denying four honest uncorrected exceedances is the same sin as printing the most extreme cell. It now reports them and names the correction as the reason they are not findings. WHAT DID NOT MOVE: the served games[].pick objects and the champion product record are byte-identical before and after, verified by hash on both payloads. This block regrades nothing, restates nothing and gates nothing — the chief still refuses to speak a pattern as a reason, because nothing has separated from chance. STILL OPEN, REPORTED NOT PATCHED: games[].analysts, games[].consensus and the chief's pattern lookup are still built from the legacy per-game entries, so the configuration the chief looks up and the table it looks it up in now come from different desks. It is inert while nothing survives correction, and it must be resolved before any row ever becomes a finding. v4/serve/desk_fit.py is likewise still fitted on the pre-re-architecture history.parquet.

items.title: The history board stops repeating itself 392 times
items.tagline: The past-games payload had grown to 7.75 MB and its Supabase upload was intermittently timing out. 4.40 MB of it was one block — the desk chief's frame — written out once per game, mostly identical every time. It is now written once.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: shipped and verified end to end. THE SYMPTOM: sync_unified_history.sh returned HTTP 500 / Postgres 57014 'canceling statement due to statement timeout' — twice on 2026-07-31 alone, recovering in between, which is the dangerous shape: an intermittent failure on a job that retries never makes the published row look stale, so the job walks up to a hard limit invisibly. THE CAUSE was size. games[].diamondedge was 4.40 MB of a 7.75 MB payload, and almost all of that was repetition rather than content: the rolling desk-fit block (5.2 KB, byte-identical on all 392 cards, and ALREADY served once at analyst_desk_spec.rolling_desk_fit), four paragraphs of invariant prose, and thirteen chief fields that are byte-identical copies of the field of the same name one level up. THE FIX is a projection applied to the history board only, on two structural rules and no third: drop a key if it is a byte-identical duplicate of a surviving sibling, or if it is card-invariant and published once at the root. Every dropped byte is still readable in the same payload without another request, and the payload publishes the map — analyst_desk_spec.history_projection names each dropped key and where it now lives. RESULT: 10.39 MB to 5.73 MB on disk, 7.37 MB to 3.76 MB of actual JSON, a 49% cut; the upload now completes in about 4 seconds with no retry. The live board and single-game detail still carry the full frame — this was never an editorial decision about what a past game deserves to say.
items.detail: NOTHING'S VALUE CHANGED. The served games[].pick objects hash byte-identically before and after on both boards, as does the champion product record; the only difference across the whole 392-game payload after a round trip through Supabase is one driver value where Postgres normalised -0.0 to 0.0. The selftest proves the projection from both ends on real data every build: on the live board it takes each full card, projects it, and asserts every dropped key is recoverable (a duplicate that is still a duplicate, a constant that is still that constant); on the history board it asserts the projection was applied, that every pointer the payload publishes resolves, and that re-applying it changes nothing. A field that quietly stops being a duplicate fails the build instead of vanishing. The sync script also gained three attempts with widening backoff — belt, not braces; gzip was considered and rejected because PostgREST does not negotiate a compressed request body and the timeout is database-side work on the JSONB, not transfer time.

items.title: A sync that dies into a log nobody opens is now a failure the guard reports
items.tagline: The history sync had been failing into an error file nothing read, while the in-repo copy of its schedule pointed at a log path that stopped being written on 2026-07-23. Tailing it looked exactly like nine days of silent death.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: shipped. TWO SEPARATE HOLES, one symptom. (1) The published-freshness rail added earlier today measures each Supabase key's updated_at, which is the right question but only goes red once EVERY attempt in the window fails; a job retrying every five minutes that fails ten times and succeeds on the eleventh never looks stale, so an intermittent statement timeout is invisible right up until it stops recovering. (2) The launchd plists installed in ~/Library/LaunchAgents were repointed to ~/Library/Logs/diamondedge-sync/ on 2026-07-24, but the copies checked into diamondedge/scripts/launchd/ still named the old path under ~/Desktop — so the log a person naturally opens froze on 2026-07-23 and has been indistinguishable from a dead job ever since. That drift is what made this read as nine days of silent failure; the real log shows the job succeeded on every day from 07-24 to 07-31, with two genuine timeout failures on 07-31. THE RAIL now reads each INSTALLED plist (the truth about where the job actually writes), goes to that error stream, and FAILS when a failure is newer than the last success, WARNS when a job failed within the last day but recovered — the thin-margin early warning — and FAILS on the plist drift itself, so 'you are reading a dead file' can never again be a nine-day mystery. The repo plists were resynced to the installed ones; the rail found the drift within a minute of being written.
items.detail: Six selftests drive the rail off synthetic plists and synthetic logs in a temp directory, so the logic is proven without depending on the state of the real fleet: a failure newer than the last success, a healthy job, a recovered-but-failed-today job, a failure from days ago that healed, log-path drift, and a job with no installed plist at all. The lesson generalises: the published-freshness rail answers 'is the row the site reads being refreshed', and this one answers 'is the thing that refreshes it reporting errors nobody is reading'. Neither subsumes the other, and the failure that prompted both was invisible to each on its own.

items.title: The consensus table stops describing four analysts that no longer exist
items.tagline: record.consensus_history still derived its four sides from the old per-analyst ledgers after the analysts were re-architected. It now reads the v2 stream — and the honest answer is still that nothing here beats a coin flip.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: repointed. The four analysts were re-architected onto disjoint feature slices (SCOUT the arms, NOVA the bats, ATLAS the conditions, VEGA the price), retrained through 2026-06-30 with records restarting 2026-07-01, and their reads moved to analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date(). This table was still assembling its four sides from the champion ledger, the model grid, the simulator stream and the fundamentals stream — four models that no longer exist. It now reads the published chief contract and nothing else. THE TABLE, on 111 games where all four v2 analysts filed a read: UNANIMOUS 9-11-3 (45.0%, 95% CI 23.1-68.5%), MAJORITY 25-29-1 (46.3%, 41.1-60.4%), SPLIT 10-22-1 (31.3%, 16.1-50.0%). All sixteen configurations now occur and every one is rendered with its own n and interval. THE HEADLINE IS A NULL: across the 19 rows the table renders, ZERO survive Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.10 and every row's own 95% interval spans 50%. The lowest raw p is SPLIT at 0.050, which is what testing nineteen overlapping buckets at 95% produces by chance and is exactly why the correction exists.
items.detail: WHAT THIS TABLE DOES NOT SHOW, stated so nobody reads it wrong. The buckets look nothing like their predecessors, and that is the re-architecture working as designed, not a result: the four analysts were deliberately decorrelated, side agreement fell from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57, and all sixteen configurations now occur where most previously never did. A differently populated bucket is not a better or worse one. The only things in this block that speak to accuracy are the intervals and the family-wide correction, and both say nothing survives. Note also what did NOT change: the results being bucketed are still the served unified pick's own graded results, straight off the ledger. This block re-labels already-graded outcomes — it regrades nothing, restates nothing, touches games[].pick nowhere, and gates nothing today. SPLIT at 31.3% is the row that will tempt a reader; it is n=32 decided, its interval reaches 50.0%, and it did not survive correction. items.title: The card stops arguing with itself — AVOID now means “no bet” and nothing else
items.tagline: DiamondEdge was serving a staked bet and, on the same card, telling you the desk was passing on it. It did that on both of today's bets. The action now follows the ticket.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: shipped. THE DEFECT, measured on today's served board: all 16 games read AVOID, including game 824486 (PIT @ CIN), where the product served a real 2★ under 7.5 at +106 and the chief said “the desk leans over against the engine's under — we're passing.” THE CAUSE was not a bug in one branch; it was the whole rule. The action was decided by a four-way analyst VOTE, and (a) the served pick's own side IS one of those four voices — the unified pick comes from the grid, NOVA's engine family — so the vote is structurally the picking engine against the other three, and (b) FULL COVERAGE, activated 2026-07-30, gave all four analysts a forced read on EVERY game where previously most abstained and the “majority” was usually the picking engine alone. Under independence the other three outvote it about half the time, on divergences that are coin flips (VEGA's coverage read is capped at conviction 0.53 and flagged low_conviction; its median divergence on today's board is 1.6 points). THE HISTORICAL DISTRIBUTION shows the change precisely: over the 61 board days before full coverage, 174 of 186 served picks (94%) displayed as LEAN and all 12 AVOIDs were 2-2 splits; from the 2026-07-30 activation onward it flipped to 3 AVOID against 1 LEAN, i.e. three of four served bets telling the reader we were passing on them. THE FIX is a semantic one: AVOID now means, and only ever means, THAT NO BET WAS SERVED. A served bet displays PLAY (3★+) or LEAN (below), grounded in the star tier — the one confidence ladder on this product with an actual measured calibration — and never in the consensus configuration, because across 2,972 games no configuration separates from chance. The desk's disagreement did not disappear: it moved to `desk_agreement` (ALIGNED / MIXED / AGAINST / PENDING / NO_BET) and is spoken in the rationale as CONTEXT — “the desk disagrees: three of the four analysts lean over… that disagreement is context, not a veto” — which is worth reading and is not a contradiction. Two further incoherences went with it: the chief's O/U call used to be the desk MAJORITY (so it printed an OVER call above an UNDER ticket) and its line used to be the locked pregame total (so it printed 8.0 above an under-7.5 ticket); both are now the ticket's own side and the ticket's own line, with the pregame total carried beside them and flagged when they differ.
items.detail: THE INVARIANT AND HOW IT IS HELD. `action == 'AVOID'` if and only if `pick.status != 'PICK'` — both directions, no third meaning. It is asserted exhaustively in v4/serve/analyst_desk.py's selftest across all 810 reachable served-bet combinations (3^4 desk configurations x five star tiers x both sides): zero display AVOID, and zero contain passing language anywhere in the rationale (the test greps for “we're passing”, “the desk passes”, “we pass”, “an easy pass”, “passing on”). The mirror test runs the 1,620 no-bet combinations and requires AVOID on every one — the standing rail that a PASS can never become a PLAY is now enforced BEFORE any other rule is consulted rather than as an outcome of the vote. The serving layer re-asserts both on the real payloads. THE PATTERN RAIL IS UNCHANGED IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS: a measured configuration that survived correction can still move a displayed action DOWN one rung and never up — but on a served bet the ladder now bottoms out at LEAN, because a bet is a bet. Nothing about the served product moved: every one of the 391 `pick` objects in the historical payload is byte-identical before and after this change, the record stays 85-95-6, and no pick was created, re-priced, re-graded or removed. A new chief.coherence block reconciles the card's other voices — the desk majority, the weighted combination and ATLAS's predicted final score — against the ticket, marking each `same` or `opposite`, so a disagreement reads as information rather than as a card that cannot make up its mind.
items.result: Today's 15-game board went from 16 of 16 AVOID (including both live tickets, measured on the 19:48Z payload) to 13 AVOID — every one a game where nothing cleared the price gate — plus 2 bets: a 3★ PLAY (desk split, said so) and a 2★ LEAN (desk against, said so). Across the full 392-game historical payload: 202 AVOID, all genuinely no-bet; 147 PLAY; 41 LEAN; and zero served bets displayed as a pass. Every one of the 391 `pick` objects common to the payload before and after is byte-identical and the record is unchanged at 85-95-6.

items.title: The rolling 30-day desk fit — and its honest verdict
items.tagline: Leon asked for a best-fit over the last 30 days instead of a vote count. It is built, it is refit every night, and it reports that fitted weights do not beat weighting the analysts equally — so the desk weights them equally and says so.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: shipped as a MEASUREMENT with a null verdict. v4/serve/desk_fit.py re-fits nightly, over a trailing 30-day window of the four analysts' own graded reads, a ridge-penalised logistic regression on top of the price: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM w_a * d_a ), where d_a is each analyst's LOG-ODDS DIVERGENCE from the number it was priced against. The market log-odds enter as a fixed OFFSET, never a free parameter, so each weight answers exactly one question — does this analyst's disagreement with the price carry anything the price does not already have? That is deliberately the STRENGTH and DIRECTION of disagreement rather than the vote: a 3-1 majority of hair-thin divergences and one analyst eight points off the number are identical to a vote and completely different here. THE SCORING IS WALK-FORWARD — fit strictly on days before the day being scored, never on it — against two baselines: equal weighting (the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence, fit on the same window, so the contrast isolates differential weighting) and the price itself. Over 860 walk-forward days and 11,786 graded games, the fitted weights are INDISTINGUISHABLE from equal weighting: delta log-loss +0.00006, 95% day-clustered bootstrap CI [-0.00009, +0.00021]. Neither beats the price; at lighter penalties the combined desk is measurably WORSE than the number (equal vs market -0.00154, CI [-0.00279, -0.00027]), and the side either version takes against the market hits 50.2-50.5%. The verdict is therefore equal_weight_fallback, published with the numbers and the reason. The current live window makes the point twice over: the trailing 30 days hold 169 graded games with 23 / 25 / 150 / 6 reads for VEGA / ATLAS / NOVA / SCOUT, against floors of 300 games and 100 reads each — nowhere near enough to fit four weights, and the fitted point estimates (0.004 to 0.016) sit inside standard errors of 0.20.
items.detail: WHY IT SHIPS AS A NULL RATHER THAN AS A FEATURE. The four analysts sit between 48.6% and 51.0% on their own sides, the profile pass found zero measurable specialisms across 357 cells after correction, and no consensus configuration separates from chance across 2,972 games. A combiner over four correlated near-coin-flips has essentially nothing to separate, so any weighting scheme it produced would be fitting noise — which is exactly the failure mode this product spent the last two days removing. THE ADOPTION GATE is explicit and lives in code: fitted weights are used only when (a) the trailing window holds at least 300 graded games with at least 100 reads for every analyst AND (b) the walk-forward log-loss improvement over equal weighting has a 95% day-clustered interval strictly better than zero. Otherwise the desk falls back to equal weights, publishes the fitted numbers WITH their standard errors and intervals, and states in plain English why they were not adopted. The machinery is real and is proven to work: the selftest plants a known weight vector (ATLAS 0.9, SCOUT 0.4, VEGA/NOVA 0) into 6,000 synthetic games and requires the fit to recover it and its intervals to exclude zero; it then runs the same fit on pure noise and requires that NO weight separates from zero. So when the parallel re-architecture gives the four analysts genuinely distinct specialisations, the same gate opens on evidence rather than on assertion — no code change needed. Lambda is pre-specified at 25 and published with a sensitivity table at 5 and 100; all three reach the same verdict. Everything is presentation-layer: it gates nothing, sizes nothing, grades nothing, and the per-game combined probability (chief.desk_combined) is display only, reconciled against the ticket in chief.coherence and explicitly never a bet.
items.result: VERDICT: equal_weight_fallback. Fitted weights do not beat equal weighting walk-forward (delta log-loss +0.00006, 95% CI [-0.00009, +0.00021], n=11,786 games / 860 days), and the combined desk does not beat the price. The desk weights its analysts equally, the card says so, and the fit is refit every night so the answer can change when the analysts do.

items.title: The measured analyst profile — what each analyst is actually good at
items.tagline: The roster no longer describes the four analysts in prose somebody wrote. It describes them in what they have been measured to do — and today the honest answer is that none of them has a proven specialism yet.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: shipped. Every analyst now carries a MEASURED profile on the payload, built from the analyst lab's own eleven-axis error attribution on that analyst's own graded history (total band, side, park, starter quality, day/night, day of week, lead time, its own conviction, market lopsidedness, month, season). 353 cells were eligible across the four analysts — VEGA 92, ATLAS 90, SCOUT 90, NOVA 81 — each tested by an EXACT two-sided Fisher test against that same analyst's own complement, not against 50% and not against another analyst. THE RESULT IS A NULL: zero of the 353 survive one Benjamini-Hochberg pass across the whole rendered family at q=0.10. The smallest p is 0.00055 (NOVA in 2022-04, 59.2% on n=331) and it needed to be under 0.00028 to clear the threshold. 32 cells clear their own baseline on their own uncorrected interval, which is what testing 353 overlapping cells at 95% buys you and is exactly why the correction exists. So all four roster cards read: 'Nothing yet distinguishes where this analyst is strong; the axes all sit within noise of its own baseline.' That sentence IS the shipped product — the surface does not degrade to its most extreme cell and it does not render empty.
items.detail: WHY IT IS BUILT THIS WAY. On 2026-07-30 the consensus-pattern surface shipped by picking the most extreme of 41 cells and printing it as a discovery; it was torn out the same day and replaced with a null headline. This table renders more than eight times as many cells, so the same mistake would have been eight times easier to make. Six rails, enforced in code and in v4/serve/analyst_profiles.py's selftest: (1) ONE Benjamini-Hochberg pass across the ENTIRE rendered family — all four analysts x all eleven axes x every eligible cell, in a single pass, never per analyst and never per axis; (2) only BH survivors may be presented as a characteristic; (3) ordering among survivors is by EVIDENCE (smallest p, then largest n) and never by effect size — the selftest plants a smaller effect on a bigger n and requires it to lead; (4) every rendered line carries n and its exact Clopper-Pearson interval INSIDE the sentence, never a bare percentage; (5) a cell below n=100, or whose complement is below n=100, is not eligible at all; (6) when nothing survives the block SAYS SO as its headline. THE CHERRY-PICK GATE in the selftest is a purely random desk of 160 coin-flip cells whose most deviant cell sits 6.5 points off its own baseline: it must produce ZERO characteristics, and it does. BH is not a blanket veto either — a planted 62% on n=800 dropped into the same null desk does survive, and only that one line renders. The Fisher implementation is cross-checked against scipy on four tables to 1e-6. Recomputed nightly off the lab run and served as record.analyst_profiles with a documented field contract; record.analysts gains profile_headline so a roster card can render the measured one-liner beside the written persona line. Nothing here gates, sizes or creates a bet — betting confidence remains solely the champion EV gate and the star system. HONEST CAVEAT: three of the four analysts' histories reach back into the 2022-2023 DEV window their own recipes were selected on, which flatters them relative to true out-of-sample; the season axis keeps that visible instead of pooling it away. Prices are a flat -110 throughout, so every number is a hit-rate question, not an ROI claim.
items.result: NULL — 0 of 353 measured cells survive correction (BH q=0.10); smallest p=0.00055 against a 0.00028 threshold. No analyst has a measured specialism yet. The profile is a live measurement and keeps updating as history accrues.

items.title: The freshness guard can finally see what the site reads
items.tagline: Five Supabase sync scripts never stamped updated_at, so three live payloads advertised timestamps from July 19-26 while syncing every five minutes. The watchdog could not have caught a real outage on any of them.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: fixed and verified end to end. PostgREST's merge-duplicates upsert only writes the columns present in the request body, so a writer that omits updated_at leaves the column frozen at the row's original INSERT forever while happily rewriting the payload. Measured before the fix: picks_unified and picks_unified_live at 2026-07-21, research_roadmap at 2026-07-26, picks_v4_beta at 07-19, picks_v4_beta_live at 07-06 — all five syncing normally. All five writers now stamp updated_at, and a run that finds the payload unchanged sends a tiny heartbeat PATCH of updated_at alone, so the column means 'the sync last confirmed this key current' and a dead job is visible within minutes. Content age still lives inside each payload's generated_utc, so the pair distinguishes 'the writer died' from 'the writer is alive but writing stale numbers'. check_feed_freshness.py gained a published-freshness rail that reads all five keys in one REST GET and escalates through the watchdog exactly like a stale store. The research roadmap also got the scheduled sync job it never had.
items.detail: This is the second half of the 2026-07-26 lesson. That audit found the fleet checked that processes were alive and that keys were WRITTEN, but never how old the numbers inside those writes were; check_feed_freshness.py closed that for local stores. It left a subtler hole open: the freshness signal on the published rows was itself a lie, so the one number a watchdog would naturally trust was the one number that could never move. Every sync script now round-trips the column — it reads updated_at back through the REST API after each write and prints it in its own log line, so the proof is renewed every run rather than asserted once.

items.title: Better-calibrated confidence
items.tagline: The confidence number behind every score now means what it says — probabilities are re-checked against everything we've actually graded, every day.
items.latest: 07-27: live from today — served probabilities pass through a walk-forward calibration check fitted only on already-graded picks (7,001 of them). Past picks and records are untouched.
items.detail: Our research kept finding the same honest problem: the model's WIN/LOSS picking is real but its CONFIDENCE grading was not — measured out-of-sample, our probabilities ran overconfident and the star ladder didn't order results the way it claimed. This ships the fix the research validated: before a pick is scored, its probability is passed through a calibration map fitted ONLY on picks that were already graded before that day (never the day's own games, never the future). The map is deliberately humble — it can shrink or grow how boldly we disagree with Vegas, but it can never flip a pick's side and it refuses to learn 'unders are hot lately'. Practical effect: conviction is currently getting SHRUNK (the graded evidence says our disagreements were overstated), so expect fewer model picks, more honest PASSes, and scores that bunch lower. To be clear about what this is NOT: it does not create an edge and we claim none — it makes the confidence number honest, which is what the stars are built on. Old picks, scores and records are locked and never restated.

items.title: Desk-consensus corpus, 10x deeper
items.tagline: The four analysts' agreement table had 34 unanimous games. We rebuilt it with 459 — and the headline finding dissolved.
items.latest: 2026-07-30: nova walked back across 2022-2023 (407 days, leakage-audited); all-four corpus 325 -> 2,972 games; 'fade the unanimous desk' did NOT survive — and the product now leads with that null instead of a cherry-picked percentage
items.detail: The desk's consensus table asks what happens when all four analysts agree, when three outvote one, and when they split two-two. On the small corpus it looked like the desk was WORST when unanimous (41%) and BEST when split (56%) — a striking shape, but built on only 34 unanimous games. One analyst (nova) had no history before 2026, which capped the whole table. We reconstructed nova's point-in-time read for every day of 2022 and 2023 using the same engine and the same train-on-the-past-only rule, hand-auditing two reads end to end plus a deliberate-leak control. The sealed 2024-2026 data was never opened, and 2021 is not reconstructible at all. The measurement also changed how the product talks: nothing gets quoted as a reason unless it clears correction for the whole table, and the desk's agreement no longer nudges what you see.
items.result: NULL — with 13.5x the sample the shape washed out: unanimous 47.3% (was 41.2%), 3-1 majority 50.6% (was 46.0%), 2-2 split 50.0% (was 55.7%). Across 41 measured configurations not one 95% interval excludes a coin flip and nothing survives multiple-testing correction. The old surface ranked cells by how far they sat from 50% and printed the top three — a finding generator on a null table; it now serves the negative result as the headline, an empty highlight list, and every row's interval in view. The corpus stays as permanent infrastructure.

items.title: The prices we were betting into did not exist
items.tagline: Our best-price lookup took the best number across books at each book's OWN total, not at the total we were actually betting. Half the picks we served were selected on an edge that was never available.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: found, measured and fixed. 34 of 58 served graded picks had been priced better than anything real at their line (mean +0.077 decimal). Because that inflated price is what the +EV gate evaluates, mean gate EV fell from +5.29% to +1.65% at honest prices and 29 of the 58 would never have been served at all. The board went from 3 picks to 0 the day it landed.
items.detail: A book quoting UNDER 7.5 at +109 was donating that price to a pick placed at 8.0, where the real best was -105. The rule was stated correctly in the code's own docstring and never implemented. Fixed forward only: every historical pick keeps the price it was served at (write-once), unlocked pregame rows that were provably unobtainable were demoted with their evidence attached, and the historical re-pricing script now refuses to run without an explicit restate-history flag. A guard checks every priced row against the best real quote at its own line AT ITS OWN DECISION WALL - comparing at any later instant both clears real defects and condemns honest rows. The published record is preserved as served and carries a disclosure naming the defect: -15.2% as served, -18.7% at executable prices, nothing restated.
items.result: Live. The single most consequential defect found in the program: the measured edge that made these picks look like bets was substantially an artifact of the pricing bug.

items.title: Two sources must agree before a game is graded

items.latest: 2026-07-31: shipped. 280 of 280 July finals agree, and all 280 are confirmed by ESPN - a genuinely separate editorial pipeline from MLB. An offline audit of the full research corpus back to March 2022 compared 11,026 finals with zero disagreements and zero orientation mismatches.
items.detail: Grading read finals from MLB's Stats API, and the local database that looked like a second opinion was fed from the same Stats API. Agreement between them was consistent with a single source compared against itself. The rail now reconciles the label store against a same-feed replica (labelled as exactly that - it cannot catch a wrong MLB feed, only parse, join, doubleheader and gamePk-reuse bugs) and against ESPN. Disagreement means the game is not graded, not pruned, and stays on the board; a broken rail degrades to grading-with-disclosure rather than taking the cycle down. A 45-minute ambiguity guard returns no match rather than guessing when a stale first-pitch time sits equidistant between two candidate events. Champion's own value store was later added as a fourth axis - zero disagreements there too.
items.result: Live. Every outcome the records rest on is now independently corroborated rather than self-consistent.
