items.title: The four analysts re-architected onto disjoint feature slices
items.tagline: They were four engines reading the same features and landing on the same side. They are now four theories of a baseball game that cannot see each other's inputs.
items.eta: record accrues from 2026-07-01; no conclusion before the sample supports one
items.latest: 2026-07-31: shipped. SCOUT reads the arms (starters + bullpens), NOVA the bats (posted lineups + team offence), ATLAS the conditions (park, altitude, roof, day/night, umpire), VEGA the price (line, movement, dispersion). The slices are DISJOINT over all 613 columns of the feature space and the disjointness is enforced in code, not by convention: a FeatureGate raises if any analyst reads a column it does not own. Measured effect on the July window: pairwise side agreement fell from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57, and all sixteen consensus configurations now occur where a handful used to dominate.
items.detail:
WHY. The old four were four different ENGINES over essentially one market-anchored feature space. All four sat between 48.6% and 51.0% on their own sides, the eleven-axis profile pass found ZERO measurable specialisms across 357 cells after correction, and no consensus configuration separated from chance across 2,972 games. Four correlated coin-flips make a desk with nothing to say.

WHAT. Four causal channels of a baseball total — run prevention, run production, environment, price — one per analyst, with a small published formula of named levers each. Coefficients are constrained to each lever's DECLARED direction, so a lever the data contradicts is driven to exactly zero and reported as refused rather than fitted backwards.

THE ONE MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGED THE DESIGN. The first build had each analyst compare its absolute run projection to the posted line. On the July window that gave projection correlations of 0.23-0.34 (well decorrelated) but SIDE agreement of 0.84-0.89 (not decorrelated at all) — because a projection built from a quarter of the information has a standard deviation of ~0.3 runs while the line has 1.12, so the LINE decided every side. Each analyst now bets its own channel's DEVIATION from a contemporaneous baseline instead, and the line does not enter the side decision at all.

WHAT IT IS NOT. Not an accuracy claim. A single slice is structurally worse than the market at guessing a total, and the honest prior for any of these on its own side is ~50%, which loses at -110. The claim being made is DECORRELATION, and even that needs forward evidence. Nothing here touches the served pick or the champion product record.

items.title: All four analysts retrained on 2025 through 2026-06-30, records restarted 1 July
items.tagline: A clean forward window bought by knowingly spending the sealed date windows.
items.eta: the forward record is the evidence; it starts at n=331 per analyst and grows
items.latest: 2026-07-31: all four fitted strictly on 2025-01-01 -> 2026-06-30 (3,748 graded games at T-3h) and every record restarted at 2026-07-01. The staked-versus-lean split is gone: one record per analyst, same fields for all four, sample size and interval printed beside every rate. First 331 graded reads each: VEGA 165-159-7 (50.9%), NOVA 158-166-7 (48.8%), SCOUT 151-173-7 (46.6%), ATLAS 140-184-7 (43.2%). No analyst shows a positive edge and none is claimed.
items.detail:
THE SEAL SPEND, STATED. This training window runs straight through the 2024-04-01 -> 2026-04-30 confirmation corpus and the 2026-05-01+ cross-book holdout. Leon chose that deliberately, in exchange for something the program has never had: a forward evaluation window that begins the day training ends and can never be re-fitted on. Every number computed on the training window is IN-SAMPLE and carries no evidential weight.

THE FENCE, PROVED FOUR WAYS. (A) the training frame's maximum date is 2026-06-30 with zero rows on or after 2026-07-01; (B) TRUNCATION INVARIANCE — every analyst refitted on a frame whose SOURCE was physically truncated at the fence before any join reproduces its shipped coefficients to under 1e-9, which is the artifact's own rounding granularity; (C) FUTURE-BLINDNESS — the same game scores identically whether the frame holds the rest of the forward window or is cut at that game's own date; (D) no column that reached any design matrix appears in the label store or matches a denial pattern.

THE JULY RECORD IS A RECONSTRUCTION AND EVERY ROW SAYS SO. These models were built on 2026-07-31, so they could not have served a read on 2026-07-05. What makes it honest rather than a backtest in a record's clothing is the fence: the models never saw July. Rows are marked reconstructed_oos or live and the mix is published.

THE STANDING HYGIENE RULE HOLDS. At n=331 the 95% interval on a hit rate is about +/-5.4 points, wider than any edge worth having. No performance conclusion is drawn in either direction, and a rate below 50% is no more a finding than one above it.

items.title: Live Claude strategy sessions, one per analyst, that cannot move a pick
items.tagline: Each analyst reasons about tonight's slate in its own voice. Five independent locks stop it inventing a number or touching a bet.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: shipped and exercised end to end on the live slate. Four sessions, one per analyst, each scoped to its own feature slice, its own reads and its own record. Of 32 real responses the validator accepted 31 and rejected 1 for quoting a contribution the game's read row does not carry.
items.detail:
THE OUTPUT SURFACE IS TWO FIELDS: a one-or-two-sentence note and a stance of concur or caution. There is no field for a side, a probability, a line, a price or a stake, so a session cannot express one.

FIVE LOCKS, each sufficient alone. (1) The pick is computed by the analyst's own formula and written write-once BEFORE any session runs; the apply path copies the row forward and only ever ADDS advisory fields. A hostile response that sets pick_side, p_over, stars, is_bet and result leaves the board byte-identical — that is a selftest, not a hope. (2) Every number in a note must be derivable from that game's own read row or the analyst's own published coefficients; the check is the same one the deterministic take-generator has used since 2026-07-30. (3) A note may only cite levers inside its own slice. (4) The prompt and the response are both scanned for the other three analysts' names and raise. (5) Caution is DOWNGRADE-ONLY and the graded ledger is written from the untouched board row, so a session cannot move a record in either direction.

TWO TRANSPORTS. The headless CLI, and the agent-file path the lab already uses. The CLI returns 401 in background jobs on this machine until `claude setup-token` is run; the transport detects that specific failure, names the remedy and falls through to the agent-file path, which needs no CLI auth and is what the first live run used.

TWO REAL BUGS THE FIRST LIVE RUN FOUND. A string-comparison validator rejected an analyst quoting its own weight to four decimals; it now compares values at the token's own precision, which still refuses every invented number. And the four sessions raced on one JSON store — all four reported success and only the last survived. The store is now written from one thread, in order, with a selftest.

items.title: SIM SAYS predicted score: medians replaced with expected runs
items.tagline: It said 4-5 on almost every game because a median of a run distribution is an integer — and the two halves did not add up to the total ATLAS projects.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: fixed. The pair is now per-team EXPECTED runs from the simulator's joint distribution, shown to one decimal, and it sums to the total ATLAS projects by construction. On the 19 games on the board the old integer pairs took 6 distinct values and 17 of 19 sat entirely inside 3-5; the new ones take 19 distinct values.
items.detail:
THE DIAGNOSIS. The displayed pair was the per-team MEDIAN of the joint simulation. Two things went wrong and the second was worse. First, the median of a count distribution is an integer, so games with true means of 3.9 and 4.4 both displayed as 4 — the effect Leon reported. Second, run distributions are right-skewed, so each team's median sits below its mean and the two errors compound: the displayed pair summed BELOW the total ATLAS actually projects on 12 of 15 games, by 0.71 runs on average and by as much as 1.72 (10.72 projected, 6-3 displayed). The desk could print a lean on an 11 beside a predicted score adding to 9.

THE FIX. E[home] = (mean total + mean margin)/2 and E[away] = (mean total - mean margin)/2, both read off stores that already existed, at the same calibrated multiplier with home-field advantage on. That is exact algebra on expectations, so the pair sums to the projected total on every game to floating point — checked at 1e-9 unrounded and inside a stated 0.105 rounding budget as displayed. No re-simulation, display only, graded nowhere, write-once.

items.title: The game card stops serving one desk and describing another
items.tagline: games[].analysts, games[].consensus and the chief's pattern lookup were the last surfaces still built from the four dismantled engines — while the table the chief looked its configuration up in had already been rebuilt on the replacements. All three now read the v2 stream and nothing else.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: the third and last round of the same repointing, and the one a reader could actually see. Until today every per-game analyst cell came from the pre-re-architecture producers — VEGA off the champion rows, ATLAS off the Monte Carlo simulator, NOVA off the v4 grid, SCOUT off the simple-8 fundamentals stream, with any gap manufactured by forced coverage — so the site served SCOUT described as THE ARMS on the roster while its game-card take talked about lineups, and ATLAS still claiming 20,000 Monte Carlo runs of every plate appearance. The identities now come from the same slice registry FeatureGate enforces, so the card and the model cannot drift apart again; the takes are regenerated from each analyst's own v2 read row through a new template library, with the existing validator asserting every number in a take exists on that row and with lever names deliberately unspeakable (a lever id carries digits the validator would have to reject). THE DEFECT THAT MATTERED MOST was not the copy: analyst_desk.pattern_for handed a configuration computed from four dead models to consensus_patterns.lookup, whose table was rebuilt on the live four this morning. It was inert only because nothing in that table survives correction, so no pattern sentence ever rendered — luck, not safety. pattern_for now REFUSES any key whose entries do not stamp source == analyst_v2_stream, which is a structural lock rather than a wiring convention: it cannot be satisfied by a legacy entry however the caller is wired, and it fails to silence rather than to a number.
items.detail: WHAT ELSE MOVED, AND WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT. Forced coverage is RETIRED with the engines it fed: it manufactured a fallback read for whichever dismantled engine had frozen nothing on a game, which guaranteed a full board by construction. The v2 stream prices a game only where its T-3h frame exists — posted lineups, the umpire, the park, a consensus total — so a seat it did not fill is now served EMPTY and payload.board_coverage MEASURES the board (n_no_reads, n_games_fully_read, n_coverage_reads structurally 0) instead of asserting it. On the live board that is 8 of 19 cards fully read; that is the truth about the feed, and filling it from another model is what this whole programme exists to stop. The consensus spread dimension is permanently empty for the same reason — the v2 stream is totals-only, so no analyst has a run-line view; the run-line CALL is unchanged and now names its actual producers (run_line_stream, margin_simulator) instead of borrowing NOVA's and ATLAS's names. record.coverage is served CLOSED rather than deleted, because deleting a record is restating one. The nightly recap now stamps its desk era AT WRITE TIME, so the two nights written by the legacy builder are labelled and can never occupy `latest`. The legacy fallbacks under record.analysts and record.analyst_profiles were CUT: a single unreadable v2 artifact would have silently swapped the roster's numbers for the dismantled engines' with nothing on the page saying so, and an explicit empty block is honest where a substitution is not. THE PROTECTED SURFACES DID NOT MOVE: games[].pick and record.headline_champion_v2 hash identically across the whole change, on all four served payloads.
items.result: Shipped. 152 desk selftests and the full unified_model suite green; games[].pick and record.headline_champion_v2 byte-identical before and after (sha256 verified on picks_unified, picks_unified_live, picks_v4_beta, picks_v4_beta_live); the history payload came in SMALLER than it went out (3.757 MB compact vs 4.05 MB before) because the same publish-once projection that fixed the chief frame was extended to the analyst cells.

items.title: The rolling desk fit stops weighting a desk that no longer exists
items.tagline: The 30-day combiner was fitting weights over history.parquet — the pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four different models — and would have applied them to the four that replaced them. Repointed at the v2 graded reads. It can now fit for the first time; it still declines to.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: v4/serve/desk_fit.py now reads the v2 stream's append-only graded ledger and nothing else. The corpus restarted with the records, so instead of ~11,800 reconstructed games it has 325 fittable ones (332 graded games minus 7 pushes, which carry no outcome), 2026-07-01 to 07-31. THE INTERESTING PART IS THAT THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS NOW MET. The trailing 30-day window holds 311 graded games against a 300-game floor and 311 reads for every analyst against a 100-read floor, so four weights CAN be fitted — the first time that has been true. They are: VEGA -0.016, ATLAS -0.035, NOVA -0.028, SCOUT -0.061, every one of them inside its own standard error (~0.196), not one separating from zero. And the gate stays SHUT, because the second condition is not met: walk-forward over 169 games and 14 slates the fitted weights are indistinguishable from equal weighting, delta log-loss -0.00026 with a 95% day-clustered interval of [-0.00145, +0.00084] — an interval wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Neither the fitted nor the equal-weight desk separates from simply using the price. So the verdict is equal_weight_fallback, exactly as before, and now for a reason that is about these analysts rather than about somebody else's.
items.detail: WHY THE WALK-FORWARD IS THIN, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. The scoring loop only starts once 150 games of prior history exist, which on a corpus 31 days old costs the first half of it — hence 14 slates. That is a fact about the age of the record, not about the method, and the fix is time. The two machinery selftests that let this gate open later WITHOUT a code change both still pass: IRLS recovers a planted weight vector (ATLAS 0.9, SCOUT 0.4, VEGA/NOVA 0 — recovered 0.92 / 0.40 / 0.06 / 0.07) and on pure noise no weight separates from zero, so a null verdict on the real desk is a statement about the desk. New rails: the training fence is enforced AT THE FRAME (not one row on or before 2026-06-30, since a weight fitted on the data these models were trained on would be a fit on training data), pushes are dropped because they carry no outcome, a selftest re-derives every divergence in the frame from what reads_for_date() serves the chief so the combiner and the chief can never describe different desks, and a STRUCTURAL check — not a grep — asserts no module-level path resolves to a pre-re-architecture store. history.parquet is left untouched on disk and simply never opened.
items.result: Shipped. The combiner can fit on the v2 corpus and reports honestly that it should not: fitted weights are not adopted, the desk weights its four analysts equally, and the numbers behind that sentence are on the payload.

items.title: The complete map of every analyst-consuming surface
items.tagline: Three rounds running, a legacy surface was found one module at a time. The enumeration is now exhaustive: every module that reads an analyst side, a consensus state or an analyst outcome, with its source named and — where it stays legacy — the reason written down.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: the repointings above were each found downstream of an incomplete list, which is a process failure, not three coincidences. So the sweep was done exhaustively instead of reactively. It found three surfaces nobody had named: unified_model.analyst_graded_picks, which assembled FOUR different legacy populations and fed the nightly recap, the head-to-head rivalry boards and the weekly standings — so ANALYST OF THE NIGHT was scoring models that no longer serve anything; the legacy FALLBACKS under record.analysts and record.analyst_profiles, which would have silently reverted the roster to the dismantled engines' numbers on any night a v2 artifact failed to write; and the static synthesis_config_v1 fallback, whose consensus_rules carry MEASURED hit rates computed over the previous desk's history. All three are repointed or cut. Two more are documented KEEPS with reasons: record.coverage is a frozen ledger of a closed mechanism (served with closed:true and describes_previous_analysts:true, because deleting a record is restating one), and the predicted score plus live_atlas remain simulator products that are display-only, graded nowhere and now flagged live_is_this_analysts_read:false so they cannot be mistaken for a v2 read.
items.detail: THE STANDING RULE THIS LEAVES BEHIND. A surface is on the v2 stream when it reads through analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date() or the v2 graded ledger, and every such module now carries a structural selftest — an assertion over its own module-level Path objects and bound modules, not a grep of its source — proving it holds no route to a pre-re-architecture analyst store. consensus_patterns had one; desk_fit and analyst_desk now do too. Modules that legitimately still read the old stores are the streams themselves (champion_v2, sim_stream, scout_stream, the model grid), which are separate live products with their own ledgers and are no longer presented as analysts; the offline lab and the history builder, which reach no served surface now that the profile fallback is cut; and the frozen coverage ledger. One name collision is stamped rather than renamed: games[].scout is the simple-8 fundamentals STREAM's block, not the SCOUT analyst's read, and now says so on the field.
items.result: Shipped. The map is the deliverable: every analyst-consuming module, its source after this change, and a written reason for each one that stays.

items.title: The desk stops being empty for most of the day
items.tagline: The four re-architected analysts priced a game only where its T-3h frame existed, so eleven of nineteen games on the live board carried no read at all. They now price every wall from T-24h forward — and an empty seat states why instead of being filled in.
items.latest: 2026-07-31: shipped. THE SYMPTOM: on tonight's 19-game board, 8 games had four analyst reads and 11 had none — consensus PENDING, 44 empty seats, for most of the day. That is a regression against a standing product requirement: the streams the re-architecture replaced priced from the T-24h wall onward, so a game a day out already had four opinions on it. TWO CAUSES, both fixed. (1) The v2 stream priced ONE wall, T-3h, so a game eight hours out was structurally unreadable. (2) It was priced only in the OVERNIGHT cycle, so a T-3h frame that appeared at noon waited until the next night — pricing now runs on every intraday cycle too. THE FIX IS GENUINE MULTI-WALL PRICING, NOT FORCED COVERAGE. Each analyst now has ONE MODEL PER WALL (T-24h/T-12h/T-6h/T-3h/T-1h), fitted on that wall's own fenced training frame over exactly the levers whose information exists there. A new module, v4/models/analyst_v2/availability.py, separates the two kinds of unavailability that were being conflated: STRUCTURAL (the posted lineup does not exist before T-3h — measured, not asserted: lineup_known is 0.0000 at T-24h/T-12h/T-6h and 0.9974 at T-3h/T-1h across 17,926 wall rows since 2025-01-01) and PER-GAME (MLB has not named tomorrow's starter; the plate umpire is assigned late), which is PROBED off the row being priced. NOVA is therefore not offered a posted-lineup lever before T-3h at all — it cannot reach for a card nobody has posted — and reads the projected card and the two offences instead, saying so in its own voice. ATLAS reads the ballpark alone until the plate assignment lands and says that too. WHAT KEEPS THIS FROM BEING FORCED COVERAGE IN A NEW COAT: a read is written only when the analyst's own inputs are genuinely populated (50% of the wall model's |beta| mass on levers actually read, minimum two); a driver whose lever was imputed to the training median is STRIPPED before anything can render it; the voice is gated on the same stamp, so no sentence can claim a lineup card or an umpire the read did not have; and an analyst below the floor files NOTHING — the seat carries a reason code and a sentence naming what is missing. TONIGHT'S BOARD: 19 games, 8 fully read, 11 with nothing, 44 empty seats -> 22 games (the board grew), 22 fully read, ZERO empty seats, 18 of them first spoken to at T-24h. NOTHING MOVED THAT WAS NOT SUPPOSED TO: the T-3h wall fit reproduces the SHIPPED T-3h artifact to 0.00e+00, so this is the same engine walked back through the day rather than a second one; record.analysts is still the T-3h read one row per game and hashes identically; the 391 history games[].pick objects common with the previous published payload hash identically (2b236df2...); record.headline_champion_v2 is byte-unchanged on both boards.
items.detail: The per-wall store is write-once per (date, game_pk, analyst, WALL) and does NOT contain T-3h at all — that wall is owned by analyst_v2_stream's board, which record.analysts is graded from, and reads_for_wall() delegates to it so there is exactly one T-3h read per game and no copy to drift. Per-wall reads are graded into their own append-only ledger and published additively; the headline analyst record is untouched. A hazard the enriched join creates is closed explicitly: the fact table is snapshotted per decision point but the enriched layer is joined fresh, so a T-24h row priced late at night could otherwise read an umpire assignment that landed at noon — every row records whether it was priced inside its own wall window, and a late-arriving class that cannot be verified from the wall snapshot is REFUSED on an out-of-window row rather than assumed. pattern_for gained a second structural gate: the measured consensus table is built entirely on T-3h reads, so a card whose four seats are a mixture of walls is refused a lookup, exactly as a legacy configuration is. Payload discipline held: the multi-wall explanation fields are live-only, the history board grows ~10 KB per game against the ~11 KB it was already growing at, and the history payload sits at 3.98 MB of JSON — well inside the statement-timeout budget the 7.37 MB incident established. Selftests: a per-wall availability fixture with known gaps (an unannounced starter, two games with no umpire, no lineups anywhere), and a check over all 5,300 stored rows that no read cites a driver outside its own read set, reads a lever its wall does not allow, or claims a posted lineup before T-3h.

items.title: The minor league
items.tagline: Ten prospect analysts, each on a different theory of where an edge might live, competing on a public leaderboard for a seat on the main desk — and built so that LEADING the leaderboard is not what earns promotion.
items.eta: records accrue from 2026-08-01; the earliest an honest promotion could happen is late September 2026
items.latest: 2026-08-01: shipped and accruing. THE DESIGN PROBLEM, FIRST. A leaderboard of ten models always has a leader — after a month one of them is sitting at 56% and it is noise. That is exactly the multiple-comparison trap this program has spent two days removing from every other surface, and a leaderboard is the surface where it looks most like merit. So the farm is built so that RANK EARNS NOTHING: promotion.evaluate_prospect has no parameter that could receive a rank, promotion.py never imports the leaderboard, and a fixture that LEADS the board at 60.4% on 48 reads is asserted to be unpromotable. It already reads true on live data: TAPE tops the board at 56.0% (95% CI 50.7-61.2%) and is not promotable, while SWING at 44.0% has an interval that also excludes a coin flip — two of ten outside 50% at the 5% level, which is what ten coin flips look like. THE TEN. Seven new channels: RELAY (bullpen innings DEMANDED vs bullpen SUPPLY, no quality lever at all), BAROMETER (the plate umpire as the entire model), CIRCUIT (rest, travel, trip depth — reading the schedule spine, which no incumbent holds), TAPE (the total repricing while the moneyline sat still — a cross-market contrast VEGA structurally cannot compute), CHALK (implied MARGIN from the run line and moneyline as a read on implied TOTAL), SWING (variance not mean — every lever a contrast between two windows, no level anywhere), ANVIL (ball-in-play exposure). Plus three ORTHOGONALISED INCUMBENT CHANNELS: FORGE, HARVEST and PRISM are SCOUT, NOVA and ATLAS's exact slices and exact lever tables — read out of engines.LEVERS at import so they cannot drift — with exactly one thing changed. THE ONE THING, AND IT IS THE REAL FINDING OF THIS WAVE. The incumbent projectors fit an ABSOLUTE run total and bet their deviation from an average game, on the intent that a contemporaneous centre removes the posted line from the side decision. It does not: the channel deviation is itself 0.509-correlated with the line, which moves 1.03 runs for every run of deviation, so the market already contains the quantity the analyst treats as its own contribution and the side is close to a function of the number. Their record is a lottery ticket on which way the month's line-conditional over/under split fell. Strip the line-collinear component out of ATLAS and July goes 43.9% -> 51.6% — the ENTIRE deficit was never its own signal. Every farm projector therefore fits `total_runs - posted line` and asks the honest question, 'is this game above what the MARKET is pricing on my channel'. MEASURED RESULT: farm signals correlate with the posted line at -0.002 to 0.125 against the incumbents' 0.509, and PRISM (ATLAS orthogonalised) reads 51.0% on the same July games ATLAS read 43.2%. THE INVERTED-CHANNEL PROSPECT WAS ASKED FOR AND DECLINED, WHICH IS ALSO A RESULT. The brief called for a pre-registered test of 'a channel is not weak but backwards'. Tested on the 3,748-game training window rather than on the July record that raised it, ATLAS's channel is worth c = -0.014 runs, t = -0.09, own-side 49.8%. There is nothing to invert, and building it would have spent a fourteenth of the family's error budget on a hypothesis already known false. The refutation is published on the payload rather than buried. EXPECTED OUTCOME, STATED IN ADVANCE ON EVERY PROSPECT: ~50%, not an edge. The residual value of the three incumbent channels measures +0.006, +0.528 and -0.014 runs and only the bats carry a t-statistic. Orthogonalising converts a lottery ticket into a truthful null, and a null you can trust is a better object than a record decided by the calendar. A selftest refuses any prospect whose thesis oversells. TWO FENCES, NOT ONE. Training is fenced at 2026-06-30 like the incumbents. But the farm adds its own stricter CONFIRMATION fence at 2026-08-01, because the ten theories were CHOSEN on 2026-08-01 by an author who had read July: July is clean evidence about a MODEL and spent evidence about a SELECTION, and a window that generated the observation cannot confirm it. The leaderboard shows July; the promotion gate refuses it, and a fixture proves a spectacular July-only record counts for exactly zero. THE BAR: day-clustered bootstrap CI (slates resampled, not games) excluding zero; Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.10 across all FOURTEEN hypotheses (ten prospects AND the four incumbents, because a prospect competes for the seat an incumbent holds — apply_bh raises on a family of any other size); an anti-trivial battery requiring it to beat the MARKET'S OWN Brier, not just its own baseline; the house drop_single_best_bet guard plus an explicit drop-your-best-SLATE guard; 60 reads across 20 slates; a prereg predating the scoring; and every scored day strictly after its own training fence. Clearing all of it writes a PROPOSAL — entering the main four needs a human-signed, hash-matching state file, the same fail-closed convention as the spread and sim engine modes. Nothing is promoted automatically, ever, and the nightly cycle does not have the gate bound in its namespace. AN HONEST TRAINING RESULT WORTH READING: RELAY had ALL SEVEN levers refused by the data — every bullpen-fatigue lever correlates with the residual opposite to its declared physics — so it files no reads at all. On a residual target a declared direction claims a lever is real AND underpriced; RELAY's zero says the market prices bullpen fatigue at least as hard as RELAY does. That is a result about the market, and the leaderboard renders it as a sentence rather than an empty row. NOT A BET, ANYWHERE: every row carries is_bet=false / never_a_pick=true and assert_not_a_pick raises on any bet-shaped field; the farm's write fence permits only four farm_*-prefixed stores no pick builder reads; record.farm is a payload LEAF. Proved by checksum in one process with the block on and off: all 411 history and 20 live games[].pick objects and record.headline_champion_v2 hash identically, and record.farm is the only key whose value moves. Payload +87.7 KB (+1.37%), 3.83 MB inside the sync cliff. Leakage audit passes five ways including truncation-invariance upstream of every derived column and future-blindness on CIRCUIT's schedule features.
